subject: Exhibit G — packaging parity & discount-floor exceptions (redline)
content:
Message 1/5
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@acmehealth.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit G - packaging parity and discount-floor exceptions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the teams were impressed. Attached is our redline of Exhibit G (pricing schedule) with two asks we need to resolve before we can present to our legal/finance committee:

1) Packaging parity: Acme uses SKU families that map across multiple product SKUs. We need a clause that ensures packaging discounts (bundle discounts) applied by Redwood will be honored across equivalent SKUs during migrations for 18 months after go-live.

2) Discount-floor exception: We are asking for a temporary broadened discount floor (3% lower than standard floor) for the first two quarters while we ramp usage during the integration period.

We attached Acme_Exhibit_G_Redline.pdf that highlights the requested language. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 18-month parity window and the temporary floor concession, or propose alternative guardrails?

Target timeline: Procurement would like a signed order form in the week of Aug 16 if possible.

Appreciate a quick reply with next steps and any internal owners we should expect.

Best,
Sara Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Message 3/5 (internal)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exhibit G - packaging parity and discount-floor exceptions

Tessa — thanks for the heads up. Quick notes from commercial/legal/pricing POV:

- Packaging parity: reasonable ask, but 18 months is long. Suggest 12 months standard with an optional one-time 6-month extension if Acme meets the agreed ramp thresholds (monthly active tokens or spend bands). We should bake the extension trigger into Exhibit G with explicit SKU mapping required in schedule A. That keeps things auditable.

- Discount-floor exception: pricing team can support a temporary 3% floor reduction, but only if we:
  * Limit to first two fiscal quarters post-go-live (we can specify dates)
  * Require a quarterly reconciliation (true-up) against committed spend; if Acme undershoots the ramp targets, Redwood can reclaim the difference as a credit or invoice adjustment.
  * Exclude third-party add-ons and marketplace margins from the floor calculation.

Action: I’ll draft a redline with the two options (12-month auto, plus optional 6-month extension) and conditional language for the floor concession. Carlos in Legal suggested discrete milestone language instead of vague "equivalent SKU" wording.

I’ll attach a redline that legal/pricing would be comfortable with.

Jordan
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Message 4/5 (internal)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exhibit G - packaging parity and discount-floor exceptions

Agree with Jordan. A couple of practical points from billing/ops:

- SKU mapping: we need Acme to deliver the SKU family CSV (column: legacy_sku, new_sku, family_id) before go-live. Without that, we cannot reliably apply parity discounts across migrations. If they cannot deliver, we propose a default mapping cadence (30 days to reconcile bundles) and hold back the parity benefit until mapping is confirmed.

- Floor concession accounting: suggest we implement the concession as a temporary pricing multiplier applied in our billing layer with a separate reconciliation row in the invoice. That way both sides have a single auditable line for the concession.

- On the true-up mechanics: prefer credit issuance (rather than invoice reversal) to avoid accounting churn for Acme. The credit can be applied to subsequent invoices within 6 months.

I updated Jordan's draft to include the CSV requirement and the invoice-row approach. See attached pricing-summary.csv for a sample mapping and the toggles we need in our billing config.

Ben
Head of Pricing Operations
Redwood Inference

Message 5/5
From: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Exhibit G - packaging parity and discount-floor exceptions

Hi Sara — thanks for your patience while we reviewed this internally. Attached is our consolidated redline (Redwood_Redline_ExhibitG_v3.docx) and a short summary of operational requirements. Summary of the compromise we can accept:

1) Packaging parity: Redwood will honor packaging parity for mapped SKU families for up to 12 months post-go-live. Acme may request a one-time 6-month extension subject to meeting the agreed ramp criteria (defined in Exhibit G, Section 2). To operationalize this we need the SKU-family CSV at least 30 days before go-live.

2) Discount-floor exception: Redwood will accept a temporary 3% reduction to the pricing floor for the first two full fiscal quarters after go-live, contingent on quarterly reconciliation. If actual committed spend is below the agreed ramp thresholds, Redwood will issue a credit equal to the over-accrued concession; credit will be applied to invoices within the following 6 months. The concession excludes third-party marketplace fees.

Next steps we propose:
- Acme signs the attached redline or provides a tracked change response to the Redwood_Redline_ExhibitG_v3.docx by Aug 12.
- Acme uploads SKU mapping CSV to the shared Drive link embedded in the HubSpot deal record.
- Once accepted, we’ll send the order form for signature through DocuSign (link included below).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/EXH-G-ACME-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-043

If those timelines work we should be on track for execution the week of Aug 16. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the redline tomorrow morning if you prefer.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
